newsitem.title: GREECE: Forward curve up on bond funding, ecu/drachma flat.
newsitem.headline: Forward curve up on bond funding, ecu/drachma flat.

text.p: Ecu/drachma was hovering around 311.60/70, depos and bonds were holding and forex forwards were up on funding for CPI-linked bonds and tighter liquidity conditions due to Thursday's forex outflows, traders said.

"Depos are steady but forex forwards are higher across-the-board with short-term implied drachma rates up 20 basis points and long-term rates up 10 to 15 basis points on funding for CPI-indexed bonds," said a dealer at a private bank.
Forex outflows at Thursday's fixing drained some interbank drachma liquidity and contributed to the rate hike, the dealer said.
The central bank sold about $150 million, 50 million ecus and 30 million marks for drachmas on Thursday's fixing, dealers said.
Greece will issue five and 10-year, 4.0 percent CPI-indexed bonds on May 19.
"Five-year conventionals are more attractive than five-year CPI-indexed bonds for someone who buys the good inflation scenario for Greece," said a senior dealer at a private bank.

Even though the tax impact on five-year CPI-indexed bonds is less than on five-year conventionals due to their lower 4.0 percent coupon but yield assessments still favour five-year conventionals, he said.
"However CPI-indexed bonds provide a good hedge against inflation and suit a class of investors," said the senior dealer.
FRNs and floating rate notes were little changed in the secondary market, bond dealers said.
The mark was quoted at 159.62/67 from Thursday's 159.740 fix, the dollar at 271.61/71 drachmas from 270.060 and the ecu at 311.59/69 from 311.400 drachmas.
Ecu/drachma is sitting tight in the narrow 311.60/70 band and the market is quiet, forex dealers said.
